Sure, let me tell you about myself. I'm Alex, and I'm a product designer from Denver. My background is four years in a health app and two years in a payments company. What do I enjoy doing most? Talking to users, and turning research into simple flows. I really enjoy finding the problem behind the problem. My biggest weakness is presenting to big groups. I used to avoid doing it. So last year I decided to give a short talk to my company every month. It's still not easy, but I'm getting better. And why this role? I want to work on products that millions of people use, and I'm interested in learning from a team that works in a trio, like yours.

Hi, it's Ananya. Last year I won an award. This year I lead a team, and I have hired four designers. So, my advice for interviews. First, look at the portfolio before the call, and choose one project to discuss. Don't try to talk about everything. Second, avoid asking questions with yes or no answers. Ask: tell me about a time when... Third, keep listening. The best candidates need time to think. And my biggest red flag? A candidate who never mentions the users. If a designer talks for thirty minutes and never says the word user, I don't need to hear more. After I hire someone, I plan to onboard them in two weeks, with a buddy from the team.
